open_questions: County CU fee: the county's live permit page lists no dollar amount; an archived county FAQ (removed) listed $136.17 ($36.70 CU + $89.97 inspection + $9.50 surcharge). Current fee must be confirmed with the RER Certificate of Use office (786-315-2660) before publishing.

A City of Miami commission fact sheet (documents.miamigov.com, File ID 1579) describes a 'Short-Term Rental permit' under Miami 21 s. 7.1.2.10 with a $100 fee added to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund and annual $100 recertification, limited to 'Residential Density Increase Areas' with a 100-permit citywide lottery cap. This was NOT found on the city's live STR/Lodging procedures page and may be a proposal, pilot, or superseded text - status and adoptive ordinance number need confirmation on municode/official agenda.

Whether a city Business Tax Receipt (BTR) is required for STR units held by individual owners (vs. operating companies) inside the City of Miami - the STR procedure says 'Obtain a Business Tax Receipt' but the BTR categories/fees applicable to individual STR hosts are not spelled out on the STR page; cross-check with the BTR page findings from round 1.

Whether the City of Miami requires a designated local contact/responsible party (like the county's 24/7 responsible party) - the city's live procedure describes the Operational Management Plan and HOA certification but no explicit 24/7 contact requirement was found on the pages opened.

Miami Beach, Surfside, and Bal Harbour have their own resort taxes and exemptions from the county bed tax - operators there face a different tax stack; those municipalities' STR rules are out of scope for this file but should be separate records.

Platform agreements: the county page lists Airbnb, HomeAway/Expedia/VRBO affiliates, and misterb&b as collecting county taxes; whether platforms also satisfy the s. 33-28 listing-duties (CU-number verification, quarterly reports) in practice is not stated - compliance monitoring vs. tax collection are separate obligations.
The 2026 city STR task force findings and any ordinances adopted after Oct. 13, 2026 are not reflected - revisit city commission agendas for enforcement ordinances affecting condo STRs.

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Dept. of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER)
requirements.applies_when: Owner or responsible party offers any dwelling unit (in whole or in part) in unincorporated Miami-Dade County as a vacation rental (rented to a transient occupant for <30 days / one calendar month, or advertised as such)
requirements.fees: unverified - the county's live permit page lists no fee figure; applications were previously accompanied by a filing fee plus inspection fee, contact the RER Certificate of Use office at 786-315-2660

forms.name: Certificate of Use application for vacation rentals (submitted online or hard copy; signed under oath)

requirements.notes: Application must include: address/legal description; owner name/address/phone; responsible party name/address/phone (must be available 24/7); platform entity contact info; statement that business + tourist taxes are being remitted (by responsible party or platform); permission from owner; whole-or-part use; insurance statement; homestead-exemption-loss disclosure; prior-year rental activity; FL DOR registration statement; DBPR license statement; compliance statement. County permit page: CU application required prior to listing/advertising on any peer-to-peer platform. Platforms may only list properties with a valid CU and must report CU numbers quarterly. Repeat violators (3+ violations in 24 months) may need a $10,000 bond. This is the vacation-rental-specific CU under s. 33-28, distinct from the general business CU/BTR recorded in round 1.
requirements.timeline: Application may be offered as a vacation rental immediately upon submission, unless and until rejected/revoked after inspection (2019 amendment); Certificate of Use renews annually; renewal barred if outstanding fines/liens exist
requirements.title: Miami-Dade County Certificate of Use for vacation rental (unincorporated)

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Dept. of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER) / Code Compliance
requirements.applies_when: Operating a vacation rental in unincorporated Miami-Dade County under s. 33-28
requirements.notes: Verified standards: max overnight occupancy 2 per bedroom + 2 per property, cap 12 (excl. children under 3); daytime cap = overnight max + 4, cap 16; overnight = 10pm-7am; Florida Building Code occupant load overrides. Responsible party reachable 24/7 (on-site or resident >6 months/yr). Written notice to guests of noise/parking/waste rules before occupancy (also posted inside). HOA/condo association notification. Guest register with names + dates, open to county inspection. CU posted inside by main entrance with responsible party contact + max occupancy. Parking: vehicles only in driveway/designated area (or street/swale directly in front); max 2 transient-occupant vehicles. Noise: county noise code applies; NO outdoor amplified sound at any time. Advertising inconsistent with CU is prima facie evidence of violation. Sexual offender/predator occupancy rules within 2,500 ft of a school (s. 33-28(D)(7)). Solid waste curbside only on collection days. Penalties per s. 8CC-10: $100 first / $1,000 second / $2,500 third+ for both failure-to-obtain-CU and standards violations.
requirements.title: Miami-Dade County vacation-rental operating standards (unincorporated)

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County RER, Business Section (collected since 2024-10-01; NOT the Tax Collector)
requirements.applies_when: Renting any living/sleeping accommodation in Miami-Dade County for 6 months or less for consideration (hotels, motels, single-family dwellings, condos, rooming houses, etc.); also applies within City of Miami
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code ch. 29, arts. V-VI; Fla. Stat. 212.0305, 125.0104; Implementing Order 04-63
requirements.fees: none published for registration; $10 for failing to file electronically and $10 for failing to pay electronically (Implementing Order 04-63, eff. 2025-10-01); late penalty 10% per 30 days up to 50%, minimum $50, plus daily interest
requirements.notes: As published by the county: 6% short-term transient rental tax = 3% Convention Development Tax + 2% Tourist Development Tax + 1% Professional Sports Facilities Franchise Tax, ON TOP of 6% state sales tax + 1% county discretionary surtax (filed with FL DOR). 2% and 1% do NOT apply in Miami Beach, Surfside, or Bal Harbour (3% applies countywide except Surfside/Bal Harbour). City of Miami falls in the full 6% county-tax zone. Prerequisites per the official page: FL sales tax number (FL DOR), county Certificate of Use for private residences, county Local Business Tax Receipt (unincorporated) or city + county receipt (within a municipality). Platforms Airbnb, HomeAway/Expedia/VRBO affiliates, and misterb&b have collection agreements with the county (per county page FAQ) - operators renting ONLY through those platforms may be exempt from county registration; any direct booking or uncovered platform triggers self-registration and remittance. This is the 'bed tax' distinct from the BTR covered in round 1.
requirements.timeline: Monthly return required even if no tax collected; due the 1st of the month following the reporting period, late after the 20th (next business day if weekend/holiday); filed via TouristExpress (services.miamidade.gov/convention-tourist-tax)
requirements.title: Convention & Tourist Tax registration and monthly remittance (county bed tax)

requirements.applies_when: Proposing any short-term rental (<30 days) inside City of Miami limits
requirements.citation: Miami 21 Code, Art. 4 Table 3; Art. 7 s. 7.1.2.1(b)
requirements.notes: Per the city's official Zoning FAQs: short-term rental is a LODGING use; allowed zones are listed in Miami 21 Article 4 Table 3. Short-term rentals are NOT permitted in T3 and T4-R transect zones (essentially single-family residential/low-density residential). In a transect zone where lodging is permitted, STR is still barred if the structure lacks a Building Certificate for lodging use. Use the city's GIS Zoning Map tool (or consult Zoning) to confirm the address's transect zone, and check overlay zones/Special Area Projects for added restrictions. A Certificate of Use is required to use any structure/premises per Miami 21 Art. 7 s. 7.1.2.1(b).
requirements.title: City of Miami zoning check: STR = lodging use; T3/T4-R zones excluded

requirements.applies_when: Converting an existing building/condo/apartment unit to short-term rental/lodging in the City of Miami (new construction is exempt)
requirements.citation: City of Miami Short-Term Rental/Lodging procedures
requirements.fees: unverified - city page lists no fee

forms.name: Short-Term Rental/Lodging Evaluation Form (PDF, 284KB) - must be uploaded as 'DOC-1 STR Evaluation Form'

requirements.notes: Verified from the official city procedure: form template must not be altered in any way; must be signed by applicant AND certified by the COA/HOA; incomplete/altered forms are rejected. Also requires knowing how many units in the building are already converted: if >25% of units are STR, the ENTIRE building triggers a Change of Occupancy to transient lodging under Fla. Stat. 509.242 and FBC Interpretation No. 179 (building/accessibility/fire-safety upgrades).
requirements.timeline: submitted via ProjectDox AFTER starting the iBuild building-permit application (Step 4 of city procedure)
requirements.title: City of Miami Short-Term Rental/Lodging Evaluation Form (HOA/COA certified)

requirements.agency: City of Miami Building + Zoning + Code Compliance departments; FL DBPR (state)
requirements.applies_when: Operating a short-term rental inside City of Miami limits
requirements.citation: City of Miami Short-Term Rental/Lodging procedures; Miami 21 Code
requirements.fees: unverified - building permit fees per city fee schedule; BTR fees per category

forms.name: Operational Management Plan (OMP) template (PDF, 219KB) - signed by COA/HOA

requirements.notes: All apartments and condos must upload an Operational Management Plan on the city's template, signed by the COA/HOA; Zoning reviews it for approval, Code Compliance may inspect for compliance. Both the CU and BTR must be renewed annually. Floor plan must show the registration desk/lobby location. The procedure explicitly requires 'any applicable county licenses' too - the City of Miami operator stacks the city procedure ON TOP of state DBPR license + FL DOR registration + county Convention & Tourist tax registration; the county s. 33-28 CU is NOT needed inside city limits (city land-use authority replaces it), but county tax obligations still apply. City BTR contacts: shorttermrental@miamigov.com, (305) 416-1100. (City BTR mechanics = round-1 findings; listed here only as part of the STR stack.)
requirements.timeline: Conversion flow: evaluation form -> confirm zoning + active CO & CU copies -> building permit via iBuild (Remodeling/Repairs; Commercial; Lodging units option) + upload documents to ProjectDox (OMP, active CU, active CO, evaluation form, data sheet w/ floor plan showing registration desk/lobby) -> plan review (incl. fire review) -> inspections -> NEW Certificate of Occupancy -> DBPR lodging license -> NEW Certificate of Use (Zoning requires copy of state DBPR license to finalize CU) -> city Business Tax Receipt; then operational
requirements.title: City of Miami Short-Term Rental/Lodging operation stack (CU, CO, DBPR, BTR, OMP, permit)

requirements.notes: UNVERIFIED - official ordinance text not confirmed: multiple 2026 news reports describe an Aug 2026 enforcement action shutting down hundreds of illegal units at The Club at Brickell Bay (1200 Brickell Bay Drive) and a Sept. 10, 2026 Commission resolution creating a 60-day short-term-lodging task force with quarterly reports on condo buildings with multiple violations, plus a focus on >25%-transient buildings. Also of note for enforcement: Fla. Stat. 509.032 generally bars cities from prohibiting vacation rentals or regulating duration/frequency (with the June 1, 2011 grandfather exception), so the city focuses on zoning enforcement rather than new prohibitions. City STR compliance contact: shorttermrental@miamigov.com, (305) 416-1100.
requirements.timeline: ongoing; news reports (Sept 2026) describe a 60-day enforcement task force with quarterly updates
